All 2,025 retries across 675 diagnostic cases preserve the preceding binary’s normalized pixels and order.

dpm_gray8.changes: Data Matrix reads Gray8 pixels directly through its existing pixel APIs. Direct-part-mark retries keep packed luminance buffers instead of expanding them to RGBA. Adaptive masks keep their original representation for morphology; retry pixels, order, attempts and recognition allowances are unchanged. Both axis-aligned and perspective sampling reject malformed layouts before accessing pixels.
dpm_gray8.scope: One prespecified texture negative, falsepositives/19.png, from the unchanged nineteen-image workload receives the same unrestricted scan and 1500 ms allowance. Exact preceding and tested binaries are compared with three warmups and twelve rotated measurements on each fixed cache domain. Completed negatives, inconclusive requests, unexpected output, latency and managed allocation are retained together. The full nineteen-image workload and retail controls are measured separately.
dpm_gray8.limits: Smaller retry buffers do not establish reliable negative completion, lower CPU use, throughput or memory capacity on unseen workloads. Managed allocation excludes native allocations. Shared-host contention can change timing and completion under fixed deadlines. All losses and slower controls are retained; these finite workloads do not establish overall superiority.
dpm_gray8.contracts: On that core, on each of .NET 10, .NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.7.2, ten raw-pixel cases cover padded Gray8 rows, rotations, mirroring, inversion, GS1 metadata, cancellation and malformed layouts. Three Gray8 perspective cases and six DPM scanner cases also pass. All 675 retries across 225 diagnostic cases preserve the preceding binary’s normalized pixels and order.

qr_finder_groups.changes: Ordinary multi-QR decoding ranks geometrically consistent finder groups from up to 24 candidates and avoids mixing finders already used by a decoded symbol in the same pass. The permissive and acceptance-predicate searches retain their existing traversal. Payload validation, polarity passes, caller deadlines and recognition allowances are unchanged.
qr_finder_groups.scope: The same frozen four-symbol QR image is decoded by the exact preceding and current qualified cores. Each fixed cache domain uses three warmups and twelve rotated measured iterations. Complete four-payload sets, unexpected output, inconclusive requests, latency and managed allocation remain visible. The complete nineteen-image batch is measured separately.
qr_finder_groups.limits: This optimization groups spatially independent symbols. It does not establish reliable recovery of deliberately overlapping codes that reuse finder patterns. The permissive search remains available. These finite image workloads do not establish overall superiority, portable latency, lower CPU use or lower memory capacity.
qr_finder_groups.contracts: On that core, four generated-image cases pass on .NET 8 and .NET 10. They cover four versions, quarter-turn rotations, repeated payloads and mixed polarity with tile scanning disabled. Repeated-payload assertions require all four decoded versions.

decode_deadlines.changes: Synchronous retail row searches reuse their active deadline, check caller cancellation at every candidate, poll the clock every 32 bounded candidates and check it before returning. Adaptive thresholds and scanline selection reuse their active deadline without reducing checks. PDF417 removes duplicate clock reads already performed at row-reader entry. Search order, hypotheses, fit tolerances and recognition allowances are unchanged.
decode_deadlines.scope: The exact preceding qualified binary and current tested core scan the same images. Paired retail batches use 87 positive requests and nine typed negative requests, three warmups and twelve rotated measurements on each fixed cache domain. All measured allocation, latency, correctness and inconclusive samples are retained. Successful warmups are not retained by PowerForge.
decode_deadlines.limits: Fewer clock reads do not establish universal speed, lower CPU use or reliable completion on unseen images. Clock polling remains bounded within synchronous candidate work; the configured allowances are unchanged. Deadline-sensitive requests can still be inconclusive and every completion loss remains visible. These finite workloads do not establish overall superiority.
decode_deadlines.contracts: On that core, two deadline-snapshot tests, all 58 retained scanner-margin contracts and four caller-ownership tests pass on each supported test framework. Captured deadlines still observe clock expiry and later caller cancellation.
decode_deadlines.profile_scope: Allocation and stack profiles use three diagnostic repetitions of the public corpus adapter. Tracing overhead and JIT warmup affect completion. Sampled inclusive stacks overlap and are not CPU utilization or ranked benchmark timings.

decode_allocations.changes: Linear decoding reuses already trimmed module arrays and builds run lengths in one exactly sized array. Format order, image sampling, polarity handling, recognition allowances and payload scoring are unchanged.
decode_allocations.scope: The exact preceding qualified binary and current tested core scan the same images. Paired retail batches use 87 positive requests and nine typed negative requests, three warmups and twelve rotated measurements on each fixed cache domain. All measured allocation, latency, correctness and inconclusive samples are retained. Successful warmups are not retained by PowerForge.
decode_allocations.limits: Managed allocation reduction does not establish lower native memory use, lower CPU use, or universal latency improvement. Deadline-sensitive requests can still be inconclusive; every completion loss remains visible. These images and controls do not establish unseen accuracy or overall superiority.
decode_allocations.contracts: On that core, all 58 retained scanner-margin contracts and four caller-ownership tests pass on each supported test framework. Caller modules stay unchanged through padding, inversion, reversal and repeated decoding.
decode_allocations.profile_scope: Allocation and stack profiles use three diagnostic repetitions of the public corpus adapter. Tracing overhead and JIT warmup affect completion. Sampled inclusive stacks overlap and are not CPU utilization or ranked benchmark timings.

retail_changes: Retail contrast recovery is unchanged in this pass. Current-core diagnostics and paired costs preserve all hypotheses, independent neighboring-row confirmation and prior image gains.

databar14_recovery.changes: GS1 DataBar-14 image recognition fits both finders and four characters independently, validates the complete symbol checksum, and preserves measured enclosed guard gaps before normalizing. The same guard invariant is enforced in stacked bottom rows. Existing APIs, payload oracles, family hints and recognition allowances are unchanged.
databar14_recovery.scope: Twelve fixed RSS-14 family images from the main corpus, with the same full-family hint for every engine. They inform the repair and are regression evidence, not an unseen holdout or an additional accuracy survey.
databar14_recovery.cost_scope: Same twelve preloaded DataBar-14 images and 1500 ms allowance, separate binary contexts, three warmups and twelve rotated measurements per binary/domain. Normal priority, fixed affinity and no outlier removal. Loading and evaluation are excluded. Recognition is recorded with time: additional correct results change completed work. Shared-host contention prevents portable latency claims; managed allocation excludes native memory.

retail_positive_cost_scope: Same 87 preloaded retail positives with identical hints, payload validation and 1500 ms allowance. Separate contexts, 3 warmups and 12 rotated measurements per binary/domain, Normal priority and fixed affinity; no outlier removal. Loading and evaluation are excluded. Correctness is recorded with cost; successful decode counts must be read alongside the timing. Managed allocation excludes native costs. All measured samples and failed warmups are retained; successful warmup samples are not retained by PowerForge.

maxicode_image.limits: One symbol per image; multiple MaxiCode instances, symbol geometry, mirrored lattices and arbitrary perspective are unproved. Planar rotation, inverse polarity and label clutter have focused regression coverage. Frozen corpus recognition and cost do not establish general or equal-accuracy superiority.
maxicode_image.evidence: Six unmodified independently authored images and original expected payloads, selected before outcomes. They now also inform permanent regression fixtures and are not an unseen holdout.
maxicode_image.text_contract: Secondary text and bytes remain exact library results. Postal, country and service fields remain typed metadata; the comparison adapter presents them losslessly in the corpus carrier string.

pdf417_negative_completion.changes: PDF417 reuses eight-run codeword fits within each thresholded image and skips offset crops whose required prefix cannot decode. It receives two weighted shares of the existing 1500 ms total scanner allowance. Candidate order, fit rules, payload validation and inherited deadlines are unchanged.
pdf417_negative_completion.notes: Across four alternating passes per domain on the same 31 negative images, completed scans are CCD0: previous [28, 29], current [31, 30]; CCD1: previous [29, 29], current [30, 28]. All individual outcomes and unexpected payloads are retained in the rotation packets.
pdf417_negative_completion.scope: Three prespecified unrestricted negative images: falsepositives-2/01.png, falsepositives-2/09.png and falsepositives/15.png. PowerForge runs 3 warmups and 12 rotated measurements per engine on each verified affinity domain. Both binaries receive identical preloaded RGBA32 images and options; loading and outcome evaluation are excluded.
pdf417_negative_completion.limits: Completion and latency depend on the unchanged wall-clock budgets and shared-host load. Managed allocation is measured separately; CPU cost, sustained throughput and portable performance are unproved. Every measured sample, warmup failure and unfinished search is retained; successful warmup samples are not retained. A lower time with an unfinished search does not establish a speed win.

datamatrix_spatial.changes: Data Matrix bounds use each row first dark pixel and only search beyond the current right bound. Components too small to enter the ordered top-eight candidate list skip corner accumulation. Pixel classification, candidate selection, payload validation and scanner allowances are unchanged.
datamatrix_spatial.scope: One prespecified unrestricted texture negative, falsepositives/19.png, from the unchanged nineteen-image decoding workload. Both binaries receive the same preloaded RGBA32 pixels and 1500 ms scanner allowance. PowerForge runs 3 warmups and 12 rotated measurements per engine on each verified affinity domain. Input loading and outcome evaluation are excluded.
datamatrix_spatial.selected_scope: The additional paired control uses three unchanged unrestricted negatives: falsepositives-2/01.png, falsepositives-2/09.png and falsepositives/15.png. The same 3 warmups, 12 rotated measurements, preloaded pixels and 1500 ms scanner allowance apply.
datamatrix_spatial.limits: This isolates one texture image and does not establish performance on other images. Wall-clock allowances and shared-host load affect latency and completion. Managed allocation is measured separately; sustained throughput, capacity and portable performance are unproved. All warmups, measurements, unfinished searches and losses remain available. The full nineteen-image comparison is reported separately.
selected_notes: CCD0: the three additional negatives take 2826.150 → 2665.373 ms (ratio 0.943), with mean completed images 2.083 → 2.000/3 and managed allocation 229.99 → 227.24 MiB.
CCD1: the three additional negatives take 2375.322 → 2191.310 ms (ratio 0.923), with mean completed images 2.833 → 2.667/3 and managed allocation 226.88 → 228.16 MiB.

code39_recovery.changes: Code 39 locates complete guarded symbols in either scanline direction and accepts quiet runs clipped only at the physical image boundary. Interior quiet-zone, character-width and payload checks remain. Fixed nine-run normalization avoids temporary LINQ arrays. RequireValid now checks short payloads and validates and strips the checksum for the encoder-supported empty payload; optional checksum behavior remains unchanged.
code39_recovery.scope: Twelve unchanged Code 39 positives from the main corpus and the same thirty-one negative image IDs with an explicit Code 39 hint. These are supplementary contract checks; they do not establish a general recognition or false-positive rate.
code39_recovery.limits: Both binaries receive identical hints, pixels, validation and allowances. The earlier binary reads fewer positive images, so latency ratios include different completed recognition work. Managed allocation excludes native costs; shared-host measurements do not establish portable speed, throughput or capacity. Every measured sample, warmup failure, completion and unexpected payload is retained; successful warmup samples are not retained.

itf_recovery.changes: ITF locates complete start/data/stop runs in either scanline direction and fits narrow and wide bars separately from spaces. Both recovered independent images pass through pixel and image entrypoints. Interior quiet zones, digit structure, ITF-14 checksums and clipped-region checks remain enforced. Codabar shares the unchanged width-fitting calculation.
itf_recovery.scope: Twelve unchanged ITF positives from the main corpus and the same thirty-one negative image IDs with an explicit ITF hint. These supplementary checks do not establish a general recognition or false-positive rate.
itf_recovery.limits: Both binaries receive identical hints, pixels, validation and allowances. The earlier binary reads fewer positives, so latency ratios include different completed recognition work. Managed allocation excludes native costs; shared-host measurements do not establish portable speed, throughput or capacity. Every measured sample, warmup failure, completion and unexpected payload is retained; successful warmup samples are not retained.

pdf417_cache.limits: Private cache checks compare every run against independently sampled pixels. Instrumented cache counts use two existing negatives, two PDF417-only passes with a 60,000 ms diagnostic allowance to complete all work; their timings are unranked. The actual baseline/current cache source is retained in the archive. Cache byte accounting is an estimate and excludes other decoder working memory; no peak-memory claim is made. The paired controls and whole-image costs preserve the 1,500 ms allowance, preloaded pixels, hints and empty oracles. Shared-host load limits portable latency and completion claims.

codabar_run_recovery.limits: Two main-corpus images informed implementation and permanent regression fixtures. Five additional upstream Codabar images were collected after the fix; all three engines already passed them on the previous binary. The 31 fixed negative inputs use an explicit Codabar hint and are contract diagnostics, not a representative false-positive survey. Main corpus, format hints, payload oracles, scoring and allowances remain unchanged. All-format costs and negative completion are separately rerun; these finite results do not establish overall superiority.

qr_exact_grid.limits: Both images informed implementation and permanent regression fixtures; they are not unseen inputs. Each is a dense version-40 raster at one pixel per module. The candidate requires exactly two grayscale levels, integer spacing, three recognizable finders and uniform pixel blocks. Ordinary photographs retain the existing fallback and bounded version search. Current main corpus, negative rotation and whole-image costs are rerun with unchanged hints, payload oracles, scoring and deadlines. This does not establish general photograph recovery or overall superiority.
qr_exact_grid.legacy_scope: The exact-raster candidate uses the existing modern pixel decoder (net8/net10); the net472 and netstandard module/fallback boundaries remain unchanged and are separately validated.
